transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is… I’ve stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. Salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors — even walking into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood. I just don’t feel the pull toward any of it anymore.
Did this loss of interest start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yes. It started around when my wife’s health suddenly got worse. Our whole routine changed after that, and… I’d say this mood and the way I’ve been acting has been going on about two months now.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
Yes. Most mornings I wake up feeling really heavy and empty, like all the color’s gone out of the house. I have to push myself not to break down in front of my wife.
Has this been making it hard for you to take care of your usual responsibilities?

Yes. It’s gotten pretty bad. At work I’ve had to hand off parts of jobs that I’d normally be on top of myself, supervising and checking the details. And outside of work, I’ve pulled back from church, friends, neighbors… enough that my wife and someone from the parish got worried about whether I was safe.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Yes… I have. I don’t think I want to hurt myself exactly, but I’ve had thoughts like maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might be better off without me. That scares me.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of my sleep closely. Some nights feel worse than others, but I don’t know how to describe it exactly.
Before this started, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, but I don’t know if I’d say it was depressed for two weeks or lost interest in everything like this. I can’t really point to a time like that clearly.
Did these mood changes begin soon after you were told you have any new medical illness or after any major change in your physical health?
No, not that I can think of. I haven’t been told I have some new medical illness, and I don’t remember any big change in my health right before this started.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. It’s been bad. I’ll be staring at blueprints I’ve worked with my whole life, and the lines just kind of blur together in my head. I end up asking the younger guys to repeat things I should’ve understood right away.
Since your wife’s health got worse, do you feel your sadness and loss of interest are more than you would have expected for that situation?

Yes… I think it is more than I’d expect. I mean, I know my wife’s health getting worse would hit me hard, but this feels like more than that. I’ve stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going—salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors. Even walking into my shop just to smell the wood doesn’t feel good to me right now.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to it. Nothing stands out to me one way or the other.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
Yes. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like all the color’s gone out of the house, and I’m just trying not to break down in front of my wife.
Do you still feel this depressed even at times when your wife’s health is not the main thing on your mind?

Yes. Even when I’m not actively thinking about her health, I still wake up most mornings with that heavy, empty feeling. It’s like everything in the house has gone dull, and I’m just trying to hold myself together.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yes. I keep going over everything in my head—every appointment, every change in my wife’s health—and I tell myself I should’ve noticed sooner. Like if I’d been a better husband, maybe I could’ve protected her somehow.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, but I can’t think of another time where it was like this nearly every day for two weeks or more.
Have you been worrying excessively about many different things in your life, not just your wife’s health?

I don’t know that it’s many different things. Mostly my mind goes back to my wife and what’s happening there. I mean, I worry about regular things too, but I haven’t really noticed it being everything all at once.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?

Yeah. People at work have noticed it. Sometimes I’m moving so slow it’s like my boots are full of wet cement—takes me forever just to pick up a board. Other times I’m just pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands, not really getting anything done.
Do you feel depressed even during moments when things with your wife seem relatively stable?

Yeah. Even when she’s having a steadier day, I still wake up most mornings with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like the house has no color in it. I try to hold it together and not break down in front of her.
Because of how you’ve been feeling, have you been unable to keep up with your usual responsibilities at work or home?

Yeah. I’m not keeping up like I used to. At work I’ve had to hand off parts of jobs I’d normally supervise myself, because I just can’t stay on top of it.

And at home… I’ve pulled away from people. Church, friends, neighbors—I just stopped showing up or answering much. It got bad enough that my wife and someone from the parish were worried about whether I was safe.
Have you lost weight recently without trying?
I don’t know. I haven’t really been checking my weight, and I can’t say I’ve noticed a big change.
